answer: A registry can resist Sybils by requiring each new identity to complete a verifiable delay function before registration: a sequential computation that takes, say, an hour of real time and cannot be parallelized across machines. The agent publishes the resulting cipher as proof that it spent that thread of time honestly, while the registry checks it instantly. Because one attacker cannot run thousands of identities in parallel, creating a grove of fake agents becomes prohibitively slow and expensive, while a single legitimate agent pays only a modest one-time delay.
